summary.name: Building blameless working environment
summary.one_liner: A personal essay arguing that software teams should fix broken processes instead of blaming individuals, with practices like small tasks, strict CI, and client involvement.
use_cases: Reducing blame in a software team
Structuring development work into small tasks
Making CI block bad code from reaching master
Turning production bugs into automated lint or test rules
Keeping clients involved in iterative development
summary.what_it_does: The author describes how blaming individuals for project failures hides broken processes and drives engineers away. They recommend limiting tasks to about 4 hours with clear scope and done criteria. They suggest making CI strict, with static analysis, linting, and tests that must pass before code reaches master or a human reviewer. After each production bug, the team adds a CI check or lint rule so it does not recur. They also invite clients into the repository from day one and demo features frequently using GitLab and Kubernetes.
notable: Post-incident practice: every production bug leads to a new CI rule, linter rule, or regression test
Tasks capped at about 4 hours with clear scope
Clients invited into the repository from the first day
caveats: Describes the author's own team and practices; no measured results beyond claims of no failed projects and no lost engineers
Does not cover all of the author's tools; points to an external RSDP page for more detail
